newsitem.title: KAZACHSTAN: Kazakh PM threatened with sack over unpaid wages.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh PM threatened with sack over unpaid wages.

text.p: Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev threatened on Monday to sack reformist Prime Minister Akezhan Kazhegeldin if he failed to tackle the former Soviet republic's large backlog of unpaid wages and pensions.

"I give April 10 as the deadline and he (Kazhegeldin) should by then tell how he will resolve this problem -- or leave," Nazarbayev told a government meeting, also attended by regional leaders and reporters.
The prime minister himself was not at the meeting.

Kazhegeldin, 45, a successful businessman before his appointment as prime minister in October 1994, is seen by Western investors as the main guarantor of market economic reforms in the vast, resource-rich Central Asian nation.
But rumours of his imminent sacking have been circulating in the Kazakh capital Almaty for weeks.
"Out of fear of the stick you can work," Nazarbayev chastised other ministers in Kazhegeldin's absence. "But without it -- despite it being your constitutional duty -- you cannot."
Observers say Nazarbayev, who enjoys strong executive powers, is concerned about his growing unpopularity among the 16.9 million population over wages and pensions, which have gone unpaid for months.
"Today I am in a peaceful mood but on April 10 we will hold a special meeting on salaries and pensions," Nazarbayev promised the assembled ministers.
His tough talking comes just as Kazhegeldin is waging a high-stakes political battle over the multi-billion dollar privatisation of the country's oil and gas industry.
Kazhegeldin favours participation of Western investors in the process while the republic's Soviet-era directors do not.

Former oil and gas minister Nurlan Balgimbayev -- the main opponent of Kazhegeldin's planned sell-off of oil and gas companies -- was appointed by Nazarbayev to head the new state Kazkakh Oil company last week.
Nazarbayev said last week Kazakh Oil would hold a 40-50 percent stake in all joint ventures with Western companies developing Kazakhstan's oil riches.
In another blow to Kazhegeldin, Nazarbayev said on Monday he had given senior state posts to two other known opponents of the embattled prime minister.
One of them, Galymzhan Zhakiyanov, has been moved from head of the country's Semipalatinsk region to lead the new Agency for Control of Strategic Resources.
Zhakiyanov's agency will oversee use of the country's oil, gas, grain, ferrous and non-ferrous metals, along with its pipeline network. Zhakiyanov will report directly to Nazarbayev.
